issues.legal_issue: A revenue entry recording land as village common land is not displaced merely because it also records possession by the owners.
material_facts: The land was recorded as village common land, and not as residential-site land, in a revenue record produced by the claimants whose authenticity was not disputed.
The same record noted that the land was in the owners’ possession according to their respective shares; the court treated this as indicating that no one else possessed it.
issues.conclusion: The notation that the owners possessed the land did not detract from its recorded character as village common land.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(g) of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, the land fell within the definition of village common land on the basis of the revenue record. An entry noting owner possession did not negate the land’s recorded common-land character.

issues.legal_issue: Land classified as village common land is not excluded on the basis of an asserted acquisition unless the required qualifying acquisition and supporting record or deed are established.
material_facts: The claimants asserted that their ancestor had acquired the land before the relevant cutoff, with some land purchased and some received as a gift.
The asserted purchase was not from a co-sharer in the village common land, and the claimants did not establish a qualifying acquisition from such a co-sharer.
The claimants did not prove that the revenue record showed a qualifying acquisition or produce a valid deed of purchase or exchange from a co-sharer.
The land was recorded as village common land.
issues.conclusion: The land was not excluded from the village common-land category under proviso (iv) to section 2(g).
issues.legal_principle: Proviso (iv) to section 2(g) of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961, requires an acquisition by purchase or in exchange for proprietary land from a co-sharer in the village common land, before the specified cutoff, and that the acquisition be recorded in the revenue record or supported by a valid deed. The asserted acquisition did not satisfy those requirements.
